=== HANDOFF #25 — 1311 landed; AC1 STILL unarbitrated, and the blocker moved again ===

--- HARNESS RUN 30857265932 (main @ `b301e7513d`, WITH 1311) ---
`collected=58`, **6 failed / 51 passed / 1 xfailed**. Dispatched only after confirming `origin/main`
contained the merged sha (it was one commit behind at submit time) and after verifying the run's own
`headSha` matched — both checks earned; the mirror really was stale.

**THE VERDICT THAT MATTERS — 39c1 AC1 is STILL NOT ARBITRATED, for a THIRD distinct reason:**

    test_outbound_epic_parent_round_trips_via_the_epic_link
    SETUP FAILED (not a rebar defect): project RBJSXPQ offers no 'Epic' issue type
    (has ['Sub-task', 'Task'])

The harness's scratch project cannot create an Epic, so the Epic Link relationship cannot exist, so
the cell cannot reach the code. Filed as [rebar:3fe5-c22e-dc2d-4c9e] (child of this epic; 39c1 and
9bb9 both now `depends_on` it). The three reasons AC1 has gone unproven, in order: the emit/apply
gates were disjoint → the greenhopper route 404'd → the fixture cannot build the fixture.

The cell reported SETUP FAILED distinctly rather than as an ambiguous red, so diagnosis cost one
grep. `_seed_epic` discovering issue types instead of hardcoding `Epic` is what bought that.

Other five reds are all previously filed and reproduced: 18a5 (no binding), 1a9f x2 (sub-task
reparent no-op, both directions), 37e7 (DC refuses the sub-task clear), and 39c1's own
`test_outbound_clear_parent_round_trips`.

--- LANDED TODAY ---
  1302 `8ab91b3f33`, 1303 `29f9627128`, 1305 `364c4e8f5e`, 1311 `b301e7513d`.
  CLOSED: 88d9, 2b16 (both `--class preexisting`), 0cfd (duplicate).
  ABANDONED: 1314 — superseded by `36e986c188`, which fixed the same hygiene refs first.

--- IN REVIEW, a 3-deep stack on `b301e7513d` ---
  **1319** 18a5 — `assert_bridge_alert_for_mutation`; takes the pass's CompletedProcess as a
     REQUIRED arg so "no alert" cannot be confused with "nobody looked".
  **1320** 1a9f — raw-REST probes (both verb forms + editmeta ops), answering AC1 without depending
     on any rebar code path. Also carries 37e7's two falsifiers.
  **1324** 9bb9 — inbound reads the Epic Link. Discovery EXTRACTED and SHARED with `set_parent`
     (`_resolve_epic_link_field_id`), not duplicated. Caught a latent bug 1311 shipped: the cache was
     a bare attribute read, which breaks for `__new__`-constructed transports — 3 pagination tests
     went red when a second caller was wired to it.
  All three verified together on current main: hygiene 0, ruff clean, mypy 421, 2105 unit tests.

--- OPERATOR RULINGS APPLIED ---
 * Criterion 11 = COVERAGE reading, but bugs filed as CHILDREN of e369, so they block closure.
   18a5, 1a9f, 37e7, 9bb9, 3fe5 are all children now.
 * Row 12's oracle AMENDED to the Epic Link + raw-REST read-back (the old text prescribed
   `pytest.raises(NotImplementedError)`, which 1311 inverts).
 * 37e7: NOT RESOLVABLE escalated → ruled "test it a different way" (non-sub-task + Epic Link),
   then found INFEASIBLE until 9bb9 lands, so 37e7 is PARKED behind it.
 * transport.py split APPROVED as its own change → [rebar:465d-c541-5e52-4e62], with a capability-
   mixin architecture rather than another rescue extraction. It is at **799/800**; nothing further
   can land in it.

--- WHAT REMAINS FOR e369 ---
 1. land 1319/1320/1324
 2. **3fe5 first** — without an Epic issue type, 39c1 AC1 and 9bb9 AC3 can never be proven
 3. 465d (transport split) before further parent work
 4. 37e7's rewrite, unblocked by 9bb9
 5. one more harness run → then close 39c1, 5200, and the epic
 6. re-run `rebar review-plan e369 --ref <sha>` immediately before the epic close (`--ref` pins it
    so it does not re-stale as main moves; it currently reads `stale-code`)

--- TWO METHOD NOTES WORTH KEEPING ---
 * Held-out TDD earned its keep twice: on 1311 two of six withheld cells caught real defects,
   INCLUDING an unguarded `.fields()` call I had made myself when I wrote the same fix inline. Two
   independent implementations, same trap.
 * My change created a VACUOUS test and a 2132-green suite hid it: a client double lacking `fields()`
   made the code decline for the wrong reason, so an assertion about epic-vs-subtask paths passed
   while testing nothing. **When a change makes production code call a NEW method on an injected
   collaborator, every existing double of that collaborator is a candidate vacuous oracle — and none
   of them will fail to tell you.**
